arguments.detail: Immediately before proto-cuneiform ca. 3300 BCE, simple tokens were gathered in discrete assemblages inside clay balls sealed with cylinder-seal impressions; on some balls, token impressions on the exterior physically and contextually match numerical signs on early numerical tablets.

arguments.detail: Small primary administrative tablets could be up to about 8 by 8 cm and divided into only a few cases; records commonly combine quantified objects with actors or offices. Numerical signs were pressed deeply with the butt ends of two round styli of different diameters, generally placing larger units before smaller units, then the object and person or office.
